module_title: Specific Transfers: Sale, Mortgage, Lease & Gift (Foundational)
introduction: This foundational level introduces the four most common types of property transfers under the TPA. It defines what happens when you sell property (Sale), use property as security for a loan (Mortgage), rent property (Lease), or give property away for free (Gift).

core_concepts.title: Sale (Section 54)
core_concepts.description:
Sale is a transfer of **ownership** in exchange for a **price** paid or promised, or part-paid and part-promised.
- Essentials: (1) Parties: Seller (transferor) and Buyer (transferee). (2) Subject matter: Must be specific immovable property. (3) Consideration: Must be 'Price' (money). If you exchange a house for another house, it is an 'Exchange' (Sec 118), not a Sale.
- Formalities: If the tangible immovable property is worth ₹100 or more, the sale can ONLY be made by a registered instrument (document). Delivery of possession is not enough.

core_concepts.title: Mortgage (Section 58)
core_concepts.description:
A Mortgage is the transfer of an **interest** in specific immovable property for the purpose of securing the payment of money advanced (a loan).
- Parties: Mortgagor (the borrower/owner) and Mortgagee (the lender/bank).
- Key Concept: Ownership does NOT transfer. Only an 'interest' transfers to secure the debt. Once the loan is paid, the interest returns to the owner.

core_concepts.title: Lease (Section 105)
core_concepts.description:
A Lease is a transfer of a **right to enjoy** property for a certain time (or in perpetuity), in consideration of a price paid (Premium) or money/service rendered periodically (Rent).
- Parties: Lessor (Landlord) and Lessee (Tenant).
- Key Concept: It transfers *possession* and *use*, but not ownership. It creates a landlord-tenant relationship.

core_concepts.title: Gift (Section 122)
core_concepts.description:
A Gift is the transfer of certain existing movable or immovable property made **voluntarily** and **without consideration**.
- Parties: Donor (giver) and Donee (receiver).
- Essentials: (1) Acceptance: Must be accepted by the donee during the lifetime of the donor. If the donee dies before acceptance, the gift is void. (2) Existing Property: A gift of *future* property is void (Sec 124).

important_entities.name: Consideration in Sale vs. Gift
important_entities.key_fact: Sale requires 'Price'; Gift strictly forbids consideration.
important_entities.significance: If an exam asks what happens if A gives B a house out of 'love and affection' but B pays A 100 Rupees in return. It is NO LONGER A GIFT. Even 100 Rupees acts as consideration, converting the transaction into a Sale (which then requires registration if the house is worth more than 100).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A heavily tested distinction. A 'Sale' transfers ownership immediately. A 'Contract for Sale' (Agreement to Sell) is merely a contract stating that a sale will happen in the future based on certain terms. Section 54 explicitly states that a Contract for Sale **does not, of itself, create any interest in or charge on such property**.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Sale = Ownership. Mortgage = Interest. Lease = Possession/Enjoyment.
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Always link the type of transaction to the exact legal right being transferred.

exam_strategy_tips: Whenever a CLAT or Judiciary question asks 'If a gift is made of both existing and future property, what is its status?', unconditionally select **Valid as to the existing property, and void as to the future property (Sec 124)**.
